newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia, Iran to revive economic commission.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia, Iran to revive economic commission.

text.p: Malaysia and Iran said on Friday they had agreed to revive a lapsed economic commission to increase economic opportunities, the national Bernama news agency reported.
The Malaysia-Iran Joint Economic Commission had not met for three years for various reasons, Bernama quoted Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi as saying.
But both countries had agreed to reactivate the joint commission with a meeting set for Tehran in November, Abdullah said.
Abdullah made the comments after receiving Iranian Vice-President Hamid Mirzadeh, who is visiting Malaysia this week.
Trade between Malaysia and Iran has increased to $320 million this year from $250 million for the whole of last year.

Ties between the countries were strengthened after Malaysian state oil company Petronas took a 30 percent stake in Iran's Sirri A and E fields in defiance of U.S.-threatened sanctions against any foreign firms that invested $40 million or more a year in the oil and gas sectors of Iran and Libya.

"Petronas has signed an agreement with Iran to conduct operations related to gas and petroleum in Iran. We will proceed because the agreement has been made...the United States can say what it likes but we will go ahead," Abdullah said.
